Investment Research Agent¶

1. Abstract¶

An autonomous agent applied to financial research depends as much on the reliability of its data sources as on the reasoning applied to what those sources return. This notebook presents an Investment Research Agent that, given a stock symbol, plans its own research steps, retrieves market and news data through registered tools, analyses that material through three specialist components, and evaluates and refines its own report before returning it. The system is built as three LangGraph workflows implementing the prompt-chaining, routing and evaluator–optimiser patterns, and exercises four agent functions: planning, dynamic tool use, self-reflection, and learning across runs through brief per-symbol notes that inform subsequent planning. All market and news data is drawn from Yahoo Finance, and language-model responses are validated against a schema wherever a result controls program flow.

Repeated evaluation established that a quality score produced by a language model is not by itself a sufficient criterion for accepting a report. Reports whose news section contained no source material scored between 0.95 and 0.99 and were accepted, because criteria that reward candour about missing information are satisfied more readily by an empty report than by a substantive one; scores rose as content fell. An input-coverage check, applied in code and held separate from the scores, was therefore introduced, and rejects a report scoring 1.00 on every criterion when no articles were ingested. A comparable defect upstream returned unreported future earnings quarters without raising an error, and was detectable only by comparison against the source data rather than from the report it produced.

The resulting agent produces grounded, sectioned reports that state their own limitations and withhold investment advice. A draft deliberately corrupted with invented figures and a buy recommendation is rejected for weak grounding and repaired to a passing report by the optimiser, and a plan generated after earlier runs incorporates instructions traceable to the notes those runs recorded. Conclusions remain limited to the data retrieved, which the system does not verify against independent sources.

2. System architecture¶

The pipeline is organised into three stages. Each stage is built as a graph of discrete processing steps using the LangGraph library, and each passes a documented data structure to the next, so the stages remain independently testable.

2.1 Pipeline overview¶

Stage names appear in each block header, the LangGraph graph implementing that stage is named to its right, and the node, tool and schema names are the identifiers used in the code that follows.

Routing is additionally exercised on its own in routing_graph, which sends a single task through route_research_task() to whichever of the three specialists the router selects. A complete review run is entered through review_and_refine_report(), which takes the research package produced by stage two.

Stage Responsibility Notebook parts
1. Data retrieval and prompt chaining Retrieve prices, company details and news; clean the text; classify and extract key facts Parts 2 to 5
2. Planning, tool use, routing and synthesis Plan the research, call the required tools, analyse news, earnings and market data separately, then draft a report and review it Parts 7 to 10
3. Evaluation and refinement Score the draft against the underlying analyses, revise it using the resulting feedback, and retain the strongest version Part 11

Wherever a step requires the language model to make a decision that controls program flow — a classification, a routing choice, a pass or fail judgement — the response is validated against a predefined schema, so subsequent steps receive well-formed values rather than free-form text. The decision to accept or reject a report is made in ordinary Python code using numeric thresholds rather than delegated to the model.

3. Workflow patterns¶

Pattern Implementation Demonstrated in
Prompt chaining Five ordered steps — ingest, preprocess, classify, extract, summarise — in which each consumes the output of the one before it Parts 4 and 5
Routing A routing component examines a research task expressed in natural language and directs it to the earnings, news or market specialist Parts 7 and 10
Evaluator–optimiser A reviewer scores each draft; an optimiser rewrites it from that feedback; the cycle repeats until the report passes or a limit is reached Part 11

4. Autonomous agent functions¶

Function Implementation Demonstrated in
Plans its research steps A planning component produces an ordered research plan before any data is retrieved Part 7
Uses tools dynamically Retrieval functions are registered as tools; the planner selects which to call, and only the selected tools execute Parts 5 and 10
Self-reflects on output quality The agent reviews its own draft for completeness and consistency; the evaluation stage then scores it against the underlying analyses Parts 9 and 11
Learns across runs A brief, bounded record of each completed run is stored per symbol and read by the planner on subsequent runs Parts 6 and 12

5. Data sources¶

All market and news data is obtained from Yahoo Finance through the yfinance library, which requires no API credentials:

  • Prices — daily closing prices over a three-month window, used to derive the current price and the 3-month change
  • Company details — name, sector, industry, market capitalisation, trailing-twelve-month revenue and trailing price-to-earnings ratio
  • Earnings — the most recently reported quarter, including estimated and actual earnings per share and the resulting surprise
  • News — recent headlines and summaries, retrieved through the quote endpoint, the headline feed, or search results, whichever responds

Because Yahoo Finance is a live service with intermittent availability, every request is retried before an error is reported, and news retrieval falls back across several endpoints. Language-model calls are made through the OpenAI API and require an OPENAI_API_KEY.

6. Reproducibility and limitations¶

The notebook is intended to be executed in order from top to bottom. Because it draws on live market data, figures and news items will differ between runs, and classifications may shift as the underlying coverage changes. An intentionally invalid symbol is included throughout the tests so that error handling is visible alongside the successful cases. A valid symbol that returns price data but no news is not treated as an error: it continues through the pipeline, and its report is rejected by the input-coverage check in Part 11.

The agent memory file, research_memory.json, persists between executions, so a re-run begins with the notes recorded by earlier executions.

The system summarises and organises information that it retrieves; it does not verify that information against independent sources, and it does not model or forecast prices. Its conclusions are limited to what the retrieved data supports, which the generated reports state explicitly.

Part 2. Market Data Retrieval¶

Retrieves price history, company details and recent earnings from Yahoo Finance.

Yahoo Finance is a live service that intermittently refuses or throttles requests, so each category of data is requested independently and retried before an error is returned. Price history is attempted through two different endpoints. Company details and earnings are requested in separate loops, so a failure in either does not discard the price data that was already retrieved.

The test at the end of this part covers three valid symbols and one invalid symbol, confirming both that real data is returned and that an unknown symbol produces a clean error rather than an exception.

In [5]:
# Price history retrieval.
# Yahoo serves the same data through two endpoints that fail independently,
# so both are attempted before an error is raised.
def _sleep_before_retry(attempt: int) -> None:
    """Wait before another Yahoo request."""
    if attempt < MAX_RETRIES:
        time.sleep(RETRY_WAIT_SECONDS)


def _download_price_history(symbol: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """Download recent price history with retry and fallback."""
    last_error = None

    # First try yf.download.
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            history = yf.download(
                symbol,
                period=STOCK_HISTORY_PERIOD,
                interval="1d",
                progress=False,
                auto_adjust=False,
                threads=False
            )

            if history is not None and not history.empty:
                if isinstance(history.columns, pd.MultiIndex):
                    history.columns = history.columns.get_level_values(0)

                return history

        except Exception as exc:
            last_error = exc

        _sleep_before_retry(attempt)

    # Fallback to Ticker.history.
    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            ticker = yf.Ticker(symbol)

            history = ticker.history(
                period=STOCK_HISTORY_PERIOD,
                interval="1d",
                auto_adjust=False
            )

            if history is not None and not history.empty:
                return history

        except Exception as exc:
            last_error = exc

        _sleep_before_retry(attempt)

    if last_error:
        raise RuntimeError(
            f"Yahoo price request failed after retries: {last_error}"
        )

    return pd.DataFrame()
In [6]:
# Assembles the full market-data record for one symbol.
# Price, company details and earnings are requested separately so that a
# failure in one does not discard data already retrieved from another.
def fetch_stock_data(symbol: str) -> dict:
    """Get stock and company data from Yahoo Finance."""
    symbol = symbol.strip().upper()

    if not symbol:
        return {
            "symbol": "",
            "error": "Ticker is empty."
        }

    # Price data
    try:
        history = _download_price_history(symbol)
    except Exception as exc:
        return {
            "symbol": symbol,
            "error": str(exc)
        }

    if history.empty or "Close" not in history.columns:
        return {
            "symbol": symbol,
            "error": (
                f"No price data found for {symbol} "
                f"after {MAX_RETRIES} retries."
            )
        }

    close_series = history["Close"].dropna()

    if close_series.empty:
        return {
            "symbol": symbol,
            "error": f"No closing prices found for {symbol}."
        }

    current_price = round(
        float(close_series.iloc[-1]),
        2
    )

    first_price = float(close_series.iloc[0])

    price_change = None

    if first_price:
        price_change = round(
            (
                (current_price - first_price)
                / first_price
            ) * 100,
            2
        )

    # Company information is separate from price data.
    info = {}

    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            ticker = yf.Ticker(symbol)
            candidate = ticker.info

            if isinstance(candidate, dict):
                info = candidate
                break

        except Exception:
            pass

        _sleep_before_retry(attempt)

    # Recent earnings are optional.
    recent_earnings = {}

    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):
        try:
            ticker = yf.Ticker(symbol)
            earnings = ticker.earnings_dates

            if earnings is not None and not earnings.empty:
                # earnings_dates is sorted newest first and includes
                # quarters that have not happened yet. Those rows carry
                # an estimate but no reported EPS, so take the most
                # recent row whose date has already passed.
                today = datetime.date.today()

                reported = earnings[
                    earnings.index.date < today
                ]

                frame = (
                    reported
                    if not reported.empty
                    else earnings
                )

                row = frame.iloc[0]

                recent_earnings = {
                    "is_reported": bool(
                        not reported.empty
                    ),
                    "date": str(
                        frame.index[0].date()
                    ),
                    "eps_estimate": row.get(
                        "EPS Estimate"
                    ),
                    "reported_eps": row.get(
                        "Reported EPS"
                    ),
                    "surprise_pct": row.get(
                        "Surprise(%)"
                    ),
                }

                break

        except Exception:
            pass

        _sleep_before_retry(attempt)

    return {
        "symbol": symbol,
        "company_name": (
            info.get("longName")
            or info.get("shortName")
            or symbol
        ),
        "sector": info.get("sector", "N/A"),
        "industry": info.get("industry", "N/A"),
        "current_price": current_price,
        "price_change_3mo_pct": price_change,
        "market_cap": info.get("marketCap"),
        "pe_ratio": info.get("trailingPE"),
        "revenue": info.get("totalRevenue"),
        "recent_earnings": recent_earnings,
        "error": None,
    }

Part 3. News Retrieval¶

Retrieves recent news articles for a symbol.

Three Yahoo Finance endpoints are tried in order, and the first that returns articles is used. This fallback exists because the quote news endpoint has been observed to return an empty list while the other two continue to serve data; without it, the news stage of the pipeline silently receives nothing.

The headline feed is preferred over search results because it supplies article descriptions as well as titles, and the analysis steps that follow depend on that additional text.

In [8]:
# News retrieval across three Yahoo endpoints.
# Each loader normalises its response into one shape so the parsing below
# is shared, and the first endpoint returning articles wins.
def _news_from_ticker(symbol: str) -> list:
    """Yahoo quote news endpoint. Preferred when it returns data."""
    return yf.Ticker(symbol).news or []


def _news_from_rss(symbol: str) -> list:
    """Yahoo headline RSS feed. Carries titles and descriptions."""
    url = (
        "https://feeds.finance.yahoo.com/rss/2.0/headline"
        f"?s={symbol}&region=US&lang=en-US"
    )

    response = curl_requests.get(
        url,
        impersonate="chrome",
        timeout=20
    )

    if response.status_code != 200:
        return []

    root = ElementTree.fromstring(
        response.content
    )

    items = []

    for entry in root.findall(".//item"):

        items.append({
            "title": (
                entry.findtext("title") or ""
            ).strip(),
            "summary": (
                entry.findtext("description")
                or ""
            ).strip(),
            "pubDate": (
                entry.findtext("pubDate") or ""
            ).strip(),
            "canonicalUrl": {
                "url": (
                    entry.findtext("link") or ""
                ).strip()
            },
            "provider": {
                "displayName": "Yahoo Finance RSS"
            },
        })

    return items


def _news_from_search(symbol: str) -> list:
    """Yahoo search results. Titles only, so this is the last resort."""
    results = yf.Search(
        symbol,
        news_count=MAX_NEWS_ARTICLES
    ).news or []

    return [
        {
            "title": item.get("title", ""),
            "summary": "",
            "pubDate": item.get(
                "providerPublishTime",
                ""
            ),
            "canonicalUrl": {
                "url": item.get("link", "")
            },
            "provider": {
                "displayName": item.get(
                    "publisher",
                    ""
                )
            },
        }
        for item in results
    ]


# Tried in order. Ticker.news stays first so behaviour is unchanged
# whenever Yahoo serves it. The other two cover the case where it
# returns nothing, which is what happens at the moment.
NEWS_SOURCES = (
    ("ticker", _news_from_ticker),
    ("rss", _news_from_rss),
    ("search", _news_from_search),
)


def fetch_financial_news(
    symbol: str,
    limit: int = MAX_NEWS_ARTICLES
) -> list:
    """Get recent financial news from Yahoo Finance."""
    symbol = symbol.strip().upper()

    if not symbol:
        return []

    last_error = None

    for attempt in range(1, MAX_RETRIES + 1):

        for source_name, load_news in NEWS_SOURCES:

            try:
                raw_news = load_news(symbol)

            except Exception as exc:
                last_error = exc
                continue

            if not raw_news:
                continue

            articles = []

            for item in raw_news[:limit]:
                content = item.get(
                    "content",
                    item
                )

                provider = content.get(
                    "provider",
                    {}
                )

                if isinstance(provider, dict):
                    publisher = provider.get(
                        "displayName",
                        ""
                    )
                else:
                    publisher = str(provider)

                url_info = content.get(
                    "canonicalUrl",
                    {}
                )

                if isinstance(url_info, dict):
                    url = url_info.get(
                        "url",
                        ""
                    )
                else:
                    url = (
                        content.get("link", "")
                        or str(url_info)
                    )

                title = (
                    content.get("title", "")
                    or item.get("title", "")
                )

                description = (
                    content.get("summary", "")
                    or content.get(
                        "description",
                        ""
                    )
                    or item.get("summary", "")
                )

                if not title and not description:
                    continue

                articles.append({
                    "symbol": symbol,
                    "title": title,
                    "description": description,
                    "published_at": (
                        content.get("pubDate", "")
                        or item.get(
                            "providerPublishTime",
                            ""
                        )
                    ),
                    "publisher": (
                        publisher
                        or item.get(
                            "publisher",
                            ""
                        )
                    ),
                    "url": (
                        url
                        or item.get("link", "")
                    ),
                    "source": "Yahoo Finance",
                    "feed": source_name,
                })

            if articles:
                return articles[:limit]

        _sleep_before_retry(attempt)

    if last_error:
        print(
            f"News request failed for {symbol}: "
            f"{last_error}"
        )

    return []

Part 4. Stage 1 — Prompt Chaining¶

Implements the first workflow pattern as a five-step chain:

Ingest → Preprocess → Classify → Extract → Summarise

Each step consumes the output of the step before it. The classification produced in step three is supplied to the extraction step, and both the classification and the extracted facts are supplied to the summarisation step.

Two of the steps return structured objects validated against a schema, so the category, sentiment and extracted lists arrive as well-formed Python values. Every step after the first begins by checking whether an error has already been recorded, and returns immediately if so, which allows a failure during retrieval to propagate without raising an exception.

A symbol that returns price data but no news is not treated as an error. It records news_error instead, the news steps are skipped, and the symbol continues with an article count of zero, so that the input-coverage check in Part 11 can reject the resulting report rather than the pipeline discarding the earnings and market data that were retrieved.

In [10]:
# Schemas for the two chain steps whose results drive later steps.
# Constraining category and sentiment to fixed sets means downstream code
# can branch on them without parsing free text.
class NewsClassification(BaseModel):
    category: Literal[
        "earnings",
        "analyst_opinion",
        "market_news"
    ]

    confidence: Literal[
        "low",
        "medium",
        "high"
    ]


class NewsExtraction(BaseModel):
    sentiment: Literal[
        "positive",
        "neutral",
        "negative"
    ]

    key_events: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list
    )

    entities: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list
    )

    key_figures: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list
    )
In [11]:
# Shared state for the prompt chain. total=False allows each step to return
# only the keys it sets, which LangGraph merges into the running state.
class NewsChainState(
    TypedDict,
    total=False
):
    symbol: str

    stock_data: dict
    articles: list

    cleaned_articles: list
    cleaned_text: str

    category: str
    category_confidence: str

    sentiment: str
    key_events: list
    entities: list
    key_figures: list

    summary: str

    # Set when price data exists but no usable news was found. Not fatal:
    # the symbol continues and the coverage check in Part 11 rejects it.
    news_error: Optional[str]

    error: Optional[str]

In [13]:
# Light text normalisation applied before the news reaches the model.
def normalize_news_text(text: str) -> str:
    """Remove simple text noise."""
    if not text:
        return ""

    text = re.sub(
        r"https?://\S+",
        "",
        text
    )

    # Apostrophes are kept so possessives and contractions survive.
    text = re.sub(
        r"[^\w\s\.,!?%$\-']",
        " ",
        text
    )

    text = re.sub(
        r"\s+",
        " ",
        text
    )

    return text.strip()
In [14]:
# Chain step 1 of 5. Retrieves the raw material and records an error that
# every later step checks, so a failure short-circuits without raising.
def node_ingest(
    state: NewsChainState
) -> dict:
    """Stage 1: get stock data and news."""
    symbol = state["symbol"]

    stock_data = fetch_stock_data(
        symbol
    )

    if stock_data.get("error"):
        return {
            "stock_data": stock_data,
            "articles": [],
            "error": stock_data["error"],
        }

    articles = fetch_financial_news(
        symbol
    )

    if not articles:
        # Missing news is a coverage gap, not a fatal error. The market and
        # earnings data are still usable, and the input-coverage check in
        # Part 11 rejects any report built without articles.
        return {
            "stock_data": stock_data,
            "articles": [],
            "news_error": (
                f"No news found for {symbol}."
            ),
            "error": None,
        }

    return {
        "stock_data": stock_data,
        "articles": articles,
        "error": None,
    }
In [15]:
# Chain step 2 of 5. Produces one combined text block for the model from
# the cleaned titles and descriptions.
def node_preprocess(
    state: NewsChainState
) -> dict:
    """Stage 2: clean the news text."""
    if state.get("error") or state.get("news_error"):
        return {}

    cleaned_articles = []

    for article in state.get(
        "articles",
        []
    ):
        cleaned_articles.append({
            **article,
            "clean_title": normalize_news_text(
                article.get(
                    "title",
                    ""
                )
            ),
            "clean_description": normalize_news_text(
                article.get(
                    "description",
                    ""
                )
            ),
        })

    cleaned_text = " ".join(
        (
            f"{article['clean_title']}. "
            f"{article['clean_description']}"
        )
        for article in cleaned_articles
    ).strip()

    if not cleaned_text:
        return {
            "cleaned_articles": (
                cleaned_articles
            ),
            "cleaned_text": "",
            "news_error": (
                "News text is empty "
                "after cleaning."
            ),
        }

    return {
        "cleaned_articles": (
            cleaned_articles
        ),
        "cleaned_text": cleaned_text,
    }

# Chain steps 3 to 5. Each prompt is paired with the node that uses it.
# The category from step 3 feeds step 4, and both feed step 5.


CLASSIFY_PROMPT = (
    ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
        """
Classify the main topic of this financial news for {symbol}.

Choose one category:
- earnings
- analyst_opinion
- market_news

News:
{cleaned_text}

Use only the news provided.
"""
    )
)


def node_classify(
    state: NewsChainState
) -> dict:
    """Stage 3: classify the news."""
    if state.get("error") or state.get("news_error"):
        return {}

    prompt = CLASSIFY_PROMPT.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "cleaned_text": (
            state["cleaned_text"]
        ),
    })

    result = (
        classification_llm.invoke(
            prompt
        )
    )

    return {
        "category": result.category,
        "category_confidence": (
            result.confidence
        ),
    }


EXTRACT_PROMPT = (
    ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
        """
The news for {symbol} was classified as {category}.

Use only the text below.

News:
{cleaned_text}

Extract:
1. sentiment
2. up to 5 key events
3. named entities
4. important financial figures

Do not add facts that are not in the news.
"""
    )
)


def node_extract(
    state: NewsChainState
) -> dict:
    """Stage 4: extract the main facts."""
    if state.get("error") or state.get("news_error"):
        return {}

    prompt = EXTRACT_PROMPT.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "category": state["category"],
        "cleaned_text": (
            state["cleaned_text"]
        ),
    })

    result = (
        extraction_llm.invoke(
            prompt
        )
    )

    return {
        "sentiment": result.sentiment,
        "key_events": result.key_events,
        "entities": result.entities,
        "key_figures": (
            result.key_figures
        ),
    }


SUMMARIZE_PROMPT = (
    ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
        """
Write a short 2-sentence financial research summary for {symbol}.

Category: {category}
Sentiment: {sentiment}
Key events: {key_events}
Key figures: {key_figures}
Current price: {current_price}
3-month price change: {price_change}%

Use only the information provided.
"""
    )
)


def node_summarize(
    state: NewsChainState
) -> dict:
    """Stage 5: write the summary."""
    if state.get("error") or state.get("news_error"):
        return {
            "summary": ""
        }

    stock_data = state.get(
        "stock_data",
        {}
    )

    chain = (
        SUMMARIZE_PROMPT
        | llm
        | StrOutputParser()
    )

    summary = chain.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "category": state["category"],
        "sentiment": state["sentiment"],
        "key_events": (
            state["key_events"]
        ),
        "key_figures": (
            state["key_figures"]
        ),
        "current_price": stock_data.get(
            "current_price"
        ),
        "price_change": stock_data.get(
            "price_change_3mo_pct"
        ),
    })

    return {
        "summary": summary.strip()
    }

Part 5. Stage 1 — Output Contract, Tools and Verification¶

Converts the final chain state into a flat record for the next stage, exposes the retrieval functions and the whole chain as callable tools, and verifies the result.

Registering the chain as a tool is what allows the planning component in Part 7 to invoke it dynamically rather than having it hard-wired into the pipeline.

The verification step requires each valid symbol to produce a complete record with a recognised category, a recognised sentiment, at least one article and a non-empty summary. The invalid symbol passes the same check by producing an error, which confirms that failures are reported rather than hidden. A valid symbol that returns no news would be marked CHECK here, since it has no category or sentiment, but it is not an error and continues to stage two. Because the data is live, the categories and figures shown will differ between runs.

In [18]:

# Registers the retrieval functions and the whole chain as tools, so the
# planner in Part 7 can select them at run time.
@tool
def get_stock_data(
    symbol: str
) -> dict:
    """Get stock and company data."""
    return fetch_stock_data(symbol)


@tool
def get_financial_news(
    symbol: str
) -> list:
    """Get recent financial news."""
    return fetch_financial_news(
        symbol
    )


@tool
def analyze_symbol_news(
    symbol: str
) -> dict:
    """Run the news analysis chain for one symbol."""
    final_state = (
        news_chain.invoke({
            "symbol": (
                symbol.strip().upper()
            )
        })
    )

    return build_symbol_profile(
        final_state
    )

# Check the final output

required_fields = [
    "symbol",
    "company_name",
    "category",
    "sentiment",
    "current_price",

for symbol, result in results.items():

    if symbol == "SPYFAKE":
        passed = bool(
            result.get("error")
        )

    else:
        has_fields = all(
            field in result
            for field in required_fields

        has_output = (
            result.get("category")
            in {
                "earnings",

            and bool(

        passed = (
            has_fields
            and has_output
        )

    check_rows.append({
        "Symbol": symbol,
        "Result": (
            "PASS"
            if passed

        ),
        "Category": result.get(
            "category",
            "-"

            "-"
        ),
        "Articles": result.get(
            "article_count",

        ),

os.makedirs(
    "data",
    exist_ok=True

output_file = (
    "data/symbol_profiles.json"

_INFINITY = float("inf")


def json_safe(value):
    """Replace NaN and Infinity with None so the file is valid JSON.

    Yahoo returns NaN for an unreported EPS or surprise. json.dump emits
    those as bare NaN, which the JSON spec does not allow and strict
    parsers reject.
    """
    if isinstance(value, float):
        is_nan = value != value

        if is_nan or value in (
            _INFINITY,
            -_INFINITY
        ):
            return None

        return value

    if isinstance(value, dict):
        return {
            key: json_safe(item)
            for key, item in value.items()
        }

    if isinstance(value, (list, tuple)):
        return [
            json_safe(item)
            for item in value
        ]

    return value


with open(
    output_file,
    "w",
    encoding="utf-8"
) as file:
    json.dump(
        json_safe(results),
        file,
        indent=2,
        default=str,
        allow_nan=False
    )

Part 6. Agent Memory — Learning Across Runs¶

Implements the fourth agent function. A short record of each completed run is stored as JSON keyed by stock symbol, and the planning step reads those records before deciding what the next run should prioritise.

Two properties are enforced in code rather than merely requested of the model:

  • The notes stay brief. Each record carries one lesson capped at 200 characters by its schema, and only the five most recent records per symbol are retained.
  • Only genuine runs are recorded. The deliberately flawed draft used in Part 11 to test the refinement loop is excluded, so a sabotaged run cannot contaminate what the agent carries forward.

The notes themselves are supplied to the planning step only. They are kept out of the report-writing and evaluation prompts, so that figures recorded earlier are not mistaken for current facts about the company. The plan that the planning step produces can reflect them, however, and that plan is passed to the drafting and self-reflection steps, so prior notes influence the report indirectly through the plan.

The store is a file, research_memory.json, and persists between executions of the notebook. Records from earlier executions therefore remain until the five-record cap displaces them.

Part 12 demonstrates the complete cycle.

In [23]:
# Agent memory: brief, per-symbol notes carried between runs.

MEMORY_PATH = "research_memory.json"

# Keep the store short. Both limits are enforced here, not left to the model.
MEMORY_KEEP = 5
MAX_LESSON_CHARS = 200


class RunLesson(BaseModel):
    """One bounded lesson carried forward to the next run."""

    lesson: str = Field(
        max_length=MAX_LESSON_CHARS,
        description=(
            "One sentence on what the next research run for this "
            "symbol should do differently or pay attention to."
        )
    )


lesson_llm = llm.with_structured_output(RunLesson)


def _read_store() -> dict:
    """Load the memory file. A missing or damaged file is not fatal."""
    if not os.path.exists(MEMORY_PATH):
        return {}

    try:
        with open(
            MEMORY_PATH,
            encoding="utf-8"
        ) as file:
            store = json.load(file)

    except (OSError, ValueError):
        # A research run must not fail because of a bad memory file.
        return {}

    return store if isinstance(store, dict) else {}


def _write_store(store: dict) -> None:
    with open(
        MEMORY_PATH,
        "w",
        encoding="utf-8"
    ) as file:
        json.dump(
            store,
            file,
            indent=2,
            default=str,
            allow_nan=False
        )


def load_memory(symbol: str) -> str:
    """Return prior notes for a symbol as text the planner can read."""
    notes = _read_store().get(
        symbol.strip().upper(),
        []
    )

    if not notes:
        return (
            "No prior research notes for this symbol."
        )

    lines = []

    for note in notes[-MEMORY_KEEP:]:
        lines.append(
            "- [{stamp}] price {price}, 3-month change {change}%, "
            "category {category}, sentiment {sentiment}, "
            "{articles} articles, evaluator score {score}. "
            "Lesson: {lesson}".format(
                stamp=note.get("timestamp", "unknown"),
                price=note.get("price"),
                change=note.get("price_change_3mo_pct"),
                category=note.get("category"),
                sentiment=note.get("sentiment"),
                articles=note.get("article_count"),
                score=note.get("evaluator_score"),
                lesson=note.get("lesson", ""),
            )
        )

    return "\n".join(lines)


def append_memory(
    symbol: str,
    record: dict
) -> dict:
    """Store one record, keeping only the most recent MEMORY_KEEP entries."""
    store = _read_store()

    key = symbol.strip().upper()

    notes = store.get(key, [])
    notes.append(record)

    store[key] = notes[-MEMORY_KEEP:]

    _write_store(store)

    return record


LESSON_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
A research run for {symbol} has finished.

Evaluator score: {score}
Accepted: {accepted}
News articles available: {articles}

Issues the reviewer raised:
{issues}

Write one sentence, at most {limit} characters, stating what the next
research run for {symbol} should do differently or pay closer attention to.

Write about the research process and the data it relies on.
Do not give buy, sell, or hold advice.
Do not predict the share price.
"""
)


def record_run_memory(
    research_package: dict,
    review_result: dict
) -> dict:
    """Derive one brief record from a finished run and store it."""
    symbol = research_package.get("symbol")

    history = review_result.get(
        "history",
        []
    )

    first = history[0] if history else {}

    issues = first.get("issues", [])

    issue_text = "\n".join(
        f"- {item}"
        for item in issues
    ) or "- none"

    try:
        prompt = LESSON_PROMPT.invoke({
            "symbol": symbol,
            "score": review_result.get(
                "final_score"
            ),
            "accepted": review_result.get(
                "final_passed"
            ),
            "articles": research_package.get(
                "article_count"
            ),
            "issues": issue_text,
            "limit": MAX_LESSON_CHARS,
        })

        lesson = lesson_llm.invoke(
            prompt
        ).lesson

    except Exception as exc:
        # Fall back to the reviewer's own wording rather than losing
        # the record entirely.
        lesson = (
            issues[0]
            if issues
            else f"No lesson generated ({exc})."
        )

    record = {
        "timestamp": (
            datetime.datetime.now(
                datetime.timezone.utc
            ).isoformat(
                timespec="seconds"
            )
        ),
        "price": research_package.get(
            "current_price"
        ),
        "price_change_3mo_pct": (
            research_package.get(
                "price_change_3mo_pct"
            )
        ),
        "category": research_package.get(
            "category"
        ),
        "sentiment": research_package.get(
            "sentiment"
        ),
        "article_count": research_package.get(
            "article_count"
        ),
        "evaluator_score": review_result.get(
            "final_score"
        ),
        "accepted": review_result.get(
            "final_passed"
        ),
        "lesson": str(lesson)[
            :MAX_LESSON_CHARS
        ],
    }

    return append_memory(symbol, record)


print("Agent memory ready:", MEMORY_PATH)

Agent memory ready: research_memory.json

Part 7. Stage 2 — Planning, Tool Use and Routing¶

Begins the second stage. Three agent capabilities appear here.

Planning. Before any data is retrieved, a planning component produces an ordered research plan for the requested symbol, along with the tools and specialists it considers necessary. The notes stored in Part 6 are supplied to this step, which is the mechanism by which earlier runs influence later ones.

Tool use. The plan names which registered tools to call. Only those tools are executed, and their results are collected into the shared state. The one exception is analyze_symbol_news: the specialists cannot run without its output, so it is added in code when the planner omits it, rather than relying on the prompt's instruction. Whether to call the two supplementary tools is left to the planner.

Routing. A routing component examines a research task expressed in natural language and returns the specialist that should handle it, together with the reason for that choice. Routing is exercised against labelled test cases in Part 10.

In [24]:
# Shared state for stage two. Each node returns only the keys it sets.
from typing import TypedDict, Optional


class ResearchAgentState(TypedDict, total=False):
    """Shared state for the Investment Research Agent."""

    symbol: str

    # Symbol profile produced by the news chain
    symbol_profile: dict

    # Prior-run notes read by the planner (learning across runs)
    memory_context: str

    # Planning
    research_plan: list[str]
    required_tools: list[str]
    required_agents: list[str]

    # Dynamic tool execution
    tool_results: dict

    # Fields backfilled from planner-selected supplementary tools
    supplementary_fields: list[str]

    # Routing
    route: str
    current_task: str

    # Specialist results
    news_analysis: str
    earnings_analysis: str
    market_analysis: str

    # Final research outputs
    draft_report: str
    self_reflection: dict

    error: Optional[str]
In [25]:
# Planning Node
class ResearchPlan(BaseModel):
    """Structured plan generated by the Investment Research Agent."""

    research_steps: list[str] = Field(
        description="Ordered research tasks that should be completed."
    )

    required_tools: list[
        Literal[
            "analyze_symbol_news",
            "get_stock_data",
            "get_financial_news"
        ]
    ]

    required_agents: list[
        Literal[
            "news",
            "earnings",
            "market"
        ]
    ]


planner_llm = llm.with_structured_output(
    ResearchPlan
)

PLANNER_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are an Investment Research Planning Agent.

Your task is to create a research plan for stock symbol {symbol}.

PRIOR RESEARCH NOTES FOR {symbol}:
{memory_context}

These notes come from earlier runs of this agent. Use them to decide what
this run should prioritise or check more carefully. They are past
observations, not current facts about the company, so do not repeat their
figures as if they were current, and do not treat them as findings of
this run.

Available tools:

1. analyze_symbol_news
   Returns processed financial news, sentiment, events,
   entities, key figures, current price, recent earnings,
   and summary.

2. get_stock_data
   Returns stock price, company information,
   valuation information, and recent earnings.

3. get_financial_news
   Returns recent financial news articles.

Available specialist agents:

- news
- earnings
- market

Create an ordered research plan.

Always include analyze_symbol_news because its structured
output is required by the specialist agents.

Choose get_stock_data and get_financial_news only when they
provide additional information required by the research plan.

Select the specialist agents needed for a complete investment
research analysis.

Do not perform the research yet.
Only create the plan.
"""
)

# Add the planning node:

def node_plan_research(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Create the research plan before executing tools."""

    symbol = state["symbol"]

    # Learning across runs: prior notes shape this run's plan.
    memory_context = load_memory(symbol)

    prompt = PLANNER_PROMPT.invoke({
        "symbol": symbol,
        "memory_context": memory_context,
    })

    plan = planner_llm.invoke(prompt)

    # The prompt asks for analyze_symbol_news, but the specialists cannot
    # run without it, so it is enforced here rather than left to the model.
    required_tools = list(plan.required_tools)

    if "analyze_symbol_news" not in required_tools:
        required_tools.insert(0, "analyze_symbol_news")

    return {
        "memory_context": memory_context,
        "research_plan": plan.research_steps,
        "required_tools": required_tools,
        "required_agents": plan.required_agents,
    }
In [26]:
# Bridges the news chain into the research workflow and decides whether
# work can continue.
# Integration Node

# Fields the supplementary stock tool can supply if the pipeline left a gap.
BACKFILL_FIELDS = (
    "company_name",
    "sector",
    "industry",
    "market_cap",
    "revenue",
    "current_price",
    "price_change_3mo_pct",
    "pe_ratio",
    "recent_earnings",
)


def _is_empty(value) -> bool:
    """True for the placeholder values Yahoo leaves behind."""
    return value in (None, "", {}, [], "N/A")


def node_load_symbol_profile(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Load the prompt-chain output into the research workflow."""

    tool_results = state.get(
        "tool_results",
        {}
    )

    symbol_profile = tool_results.get(
        "analyze_symbol_news",
        {}
    )

    if not symbol_profile:
        return {
            "symbol_profile": {},
            "error": (
                "analyze_symbol_news was not executed "
                "or returned no data."
            )
        }

    if symbol_profile.get("error"):
        return {
            "symbol_profile": symbol_profile,
            "error": symbol_profile["error"]
        }

    # The planner can also select get_stock_data. Its result fills any
    # company or price field the pipeline left empty, so the planner's
    # tool choice can affect the profile.
    merged = dict(symbol_profile)
    filled = []

    extra_stock = tool_results.get(
        "get_stock_data"
    )

    if (
        isinstance(extra_stock, dict)
        and not extra_stock.get("error")
    ):
        for field in BACKFILL_FIELDS:
            if (
                _is_empty(merged.get(field))
                and not _is_empty(
                    extra_stock.get(field)
                )
            ):
                merged[field] = extra_stock[field]
                filled.append(field)

    # article_count is deliberately not backfilled from get_financial_news.
    # It measures the articles the news chain actually analysed, and the
    # coverage check in Part 11 relies on it. Raising it from a separate
    # fetch would let a report with no news analysis pass that check.

    return {
        "symbol_profile": merged,
        "supplementary_fields": filled,
    }

# Routing: the decision schema, the schema-bound model, the prompt and
# the helper that applies them.


class RouteDecision(BaseModel):
    """Decision made by the routing agent."""

    route: Literal[
        "news",
        "earnings",
        "market"
    ]

    reason: str


# Router
router_llm = llm.with_structured_output(
    RouteDecision
)


ROUTER_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are a financial research routing agent.

Choose the specialist agent that should handle
the following research task.

Task:
{task}

Available routes:

news:
Important company events, news classification,
sentiment, and company relevance.

earnings:
Revenue, EPS, financial performance,
earnings results, and guidance.

market:
Stock price trends, recent performance,
valuation, and basic market signals.

Return exactly one route.
"""
)


def route_research_task(task: str) -> RouteDecision:
    """Route a research task to the appropriate specialist."""

    prompt = ROUTER_PROMPT.invoke({
        "task": task
    })

    return router_llm.invoke(prompt)

Part 8. Stage 2 — Specialist Agents¶

Three specialists analyse separate aspects of the same record: company news, earnings performance, and market data.

Separating them keeps each prompt narrow and makes each analysis independently inspectable. Every specialist is restricted to the data supplied to it and is instructed to state what is unavailable rather than estimate it. The news specialist is additionally instructed that an absence of articles means insufficient evidence, and must not be read as a neutral or negative signal — without that instruction a missing feed can be mistaken for a finding.

In [28]:
# News specialist. An absence of articles is defined as insufficient
# evidence, not as a neutral or negative signal.


NEWS_AGENT_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are the News Specialist Agent for an investment
research system.

Analyze only the information supplied below.

Stock: {symbol}
Category: {category}
Sentiment: {sentiment}
Key events: {key_events}
Entities: {entities}
Summary: {summary}
Source: {source}
Date: {date}
Article count: {article_count}

Explain:

1. The most important company events.
2. Overall news sentiment.
3. Why the news is relevant to an investor.
4. Any uncertainty or missing information.

- If article_count is 0 or no news summary is available,
  state that there is insufficient news data for analysis.
- Do not interpret missing news as positive, negative,
  stable, risky, or predictive.
- Do not infer future stock movement from missing information.
- Use only the supplied data.

#GROUNDING RULE
Do not introduce outside facts.
"""
)


def node_news_agent(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Analyze news-related information."""

    data = state["symbol_profile"]

    chain = (
        NEWS_AGENT_PROMPT
        | llm
        | StrOutputParser()
    )

    result = chain.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "category": data.get("category"),
        "sentiment": data.get("sentiment"),
        "key_events": data.get("key_events", []),
        "entities": data.get("entities", []),
        "summary": data.get("summary", ""),
        "source": data.get("source", ""),
        "date": data.get("date", ""),
        "article_count": data.get("article_count", 0),
    })

    return {
        "news_analysis": result.strip()
    }

Part 9. Stage 2 — Synthesis and Self-Reflection¶

Combines the three specialist analyses into a single draft report, then has the agent review its own work.

The draft follows a fixed five-section structure and is restricted to facts contained in the specialist analyses and the company reference data. The self-reflection step then assesses whether every planned research step was completed, whether each analysis is present, and whether anything appears missing or inconsistent, returning a structured assessment alongside a score.

This self-assessment is distinct from the independent evaluation in Part 11: the former is the agent judging its own process, the latter is a separate reviewer scoring the resulting report.

# Self-reflection: the assessment schema, the schema-bound model, the
# prompt and the node that reviews the agent's own draft.


class DraftAssessment(BaseModel):
    """Structured self-reflection from the Research Agent."""

    completed_steps: list[str]
    missing_items: list[str]
    inconsistencies: list[str]

    score: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0
    )

    ready_for_evaluation: bool


reflection_llm = llm.with_structured_output(
    DraftAssessment
)


REFLECTION_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are reviewing your own investment research draft.

Stock:
{symbol}

Original research plan:
{research_plan}

News analysis:
{news_analysis}

Earnings analysis:
{earnings_analysis}

Market analysis:
{market_analysis}

Draft report:
{draft_report}

Evaluate whether:

1. Every planned research step was completed.
2. News analysis is present.
3. Earnings analysis is present.
4. Market analysis is present.
5. Important data is missing.
6. Any information appears inconsistent.

Return:

- completed_steps
- missing_items
- inconsistencies
- score from 0.0 to 1.0
- ready_for_evaluation
"""
)


def node_self_reflect(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Review the draft for completeness and inconsistencies."""

    prompt = REFLECTION_PROMPT.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "research_plan": state.get(
            "research_plan",
            []
        ),
        "news_analysis": state.get(
            "news_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "earnings_analysis": state.get(
            "earnings_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "market_analysis": state.get(
            "market_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "draft_report": state.get(
            "draft_report",
            ""
        ),
    })

    reflection = reflection_llm.invoke(
        prompt
    )

    return {
        "self_reflection": (
            reflection.model_dump()
        )
    }

Part 10. Stage 2 — Workflow Assembly and Verification¶

Assembles the second stage into an executable graph and verifies its behaviour.

The graph stops immediately when the first stage reports an error, because the specialists, the draft and the self-reflection cannot produce anything meaningful without data, and running them would consume model calls to describe their own absence. Missing news is not an error at this point: a symbol with price data but no articles continues with an article count of zero, the news specialist reports that the news is insufficient, and the report is rejected by the input-coverage check in Part 11.

A separate graph demonstrates conditional routing, dispatching a single task to whichever specialist the router selects.

The tests that follow cover a full run on one symbol, routing accuracy against labelled cases, and a multi-symbol run that includes an invalid symbol to show the stop condition taking effect.

In [33]:
# Executes only the tools the planner selected, isolating failures per tool
# so one unavailable source cannot abort the run.
def node_execute_tools(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Execute only the tools selected by the research planner."""

    symbol = state["symbol"]

    tool_registry = {
        "analyze_symbol_news": analyze_symbol_news,
        "get_stock_data": get_stock_data,
        "get_financial_news": get_financial_news,
    }

    selected_tools = state.get(
        "required_tools",
        []
    )

    tool_results = {}

    for tool_name in selected_tools:

        tool = tool_registry.get(
            tool_name
        )

        if tool is None:
            tool_results[tool_name] = {
                "error": "Tool not found"
            }
            continue

        try:
            result = tool.invoke({
                "symbol": symbol
            })

            tool_results[tool_name] = result

        except Exception as exc:
            tool_results[tool_name] = {
                "error": str(exc)
            }

    return {
        "tool_results": tool_results
    }
In [34]:
# Assembles stage two. The edge after retrieval is conditional: when stage
# one reported an error the graph stops, because the specialists cannot
# analyse data that was never retrieved.
# Build the research workflow graph

def symbol_profile_ready(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> str:
    """Stop the workflow when the symbol profile could not be built.

    The news chain guards every node with an error check. This workflow
    originally had unconditional edges, so a failed ingest still ran all
    three specialists, the draft and the self-assessment, producing a
    complete report for a symbol that returned no data.
    """
    if state.get("error"):
        return "stop"

    return "continue"


research_agent_builder = StateGraph(
    ResearchAgentState
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "plan",
    node_plan_research
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "execute_tools",
    node_execute_tools
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "load_symbol_profile",
    node_load_symbol_profile
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "news_agent",
    node_news_agent
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "earnings_agent",
    node_earnings_agent
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "market_agent",
    node_market_agent
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "build_draft",
    node_build_draft
)

research_agent_builder.add_node(
    "self_reflect",
    node_self_reflect
)

research_agent_builder.set_entry_point(
    "plan"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "plan",
    "execute_tools"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "execute_tools",
    "load_symbol_profile"
)

research_agent_builder.add_conditional_edges(
    "load_symbol_profile",
    symbol_profile_ready,
    {
        "continue": "news_agent",
        "stop": END,
    }
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "news_agent",
    "earnings_agent"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "earnings_agent",
    "market_agent"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "market_agent",
    "build_draft"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "build_draft",
    "self_reflect"
)

research_agent_builder.add_edge(
    "self_reflect",
    END
)

research_agent_graph = research_agent_builder.compile()

print(
    "Research workflow ready: "
    "Plan -> Tools -> Symbol Profile -> "
    "[stop on error] -> "
    "News -> Earnings -> Market -> "
    "Draft -> Reflection"
)

Research workflow ready: Plan -> Tools -> Symbol Profile -> [stop on error] -> News -> Earnings -> Market -> Draft -> Reflection
In [35]:
# Conditional routing graph. Dispatches one task to whichever specialist
# the router selects, demonstrating routing as its own workflow.


def node_router(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> dict:
    """Route a research task to the correct specialist agent."""

    task = state["current_task"]

    decision = route_research_task(
        task
    )

    return {
        "route": decision.route
    }


def choose_specialist(
    state: ResearchAgentState
) -> str:
    """Return the route selected by the router."""

    return state["route"]


routing_builder = StateGraph(
    ResearchAgentState
)

routing_builder.add_node(
    "router",
    node_router
)

routing_builder.add_node(
    "news_agent",
    node_news_agent
)

routing_builder.add_node(
    "earnings_agent",
    node_earnings_agent
)

routing_builder.add_node(
    "market_agent",
    node_market_agent
)

routing_builder.set_entry_point(
    "router"
)

routing_builder.add_conditional_edges(
    "router",
    choose_specialist,
    {
        "news": "news_agent",
        "earnings": "earnings_agent",
        "market": "market_agent",
    }
)

routing_builder.add_edge(
    "news_agent",
    END
)

routing_builder.add_edge(
    "earnings_agent",
    END
)

routing_builder.add_edge(
    "market_agent",
    END
)

routing_graph = routing_builder.compile()

print(
    "Conditional routing graph ready."
)

Conditional routing graph ready.

Symbol:
AAPL

Research Plan:
- Analyze AAPL news for current events, sentiment, reported figures, and relevant company or market commentary; note source dates and distinguish reported facts from interpretation.
- Review recent financial news coverage for relevant AAPL discussion, including any multi-company commentary or panel debate, and corroborate material claims against company announcements, filings, or source transcripts where available.
- Retrieve current stock, company, valuation, and recent earnings data to establish an independently sourced baseline and assess whether the news changes the investment context.
- Have the news specialist assess catalysts, risks, source quality, and conflicting coverage; have the earnings specialist review recent results and guidance; and have the market specialist evaluate price, valuation, and broader market context.
- Synthesize findings across the specialists, flag stale or unverified claims, and separate current evidence from prior-run observations.

Selected Tools:
['analyze_symbol_news', 'get_stock_data', 'get_financial_news']

Selected Agents:
['news', 'earnings', 'market']

News Analysis:
### 1. Most important company events
- Apple and Meta Platforms announced a partnership to develop open-source AI, including plans to run Meta’s Muse Spark Open model on Mac products.
- Commentary considered whether the partnership could help restart the iPhone upgrade cycle. The supplied information describes this as a possibility discussed, not a confirmed outcome.
- Coverage also discussed upcoming iPhone Duo preorders and possible interest in Apple’s first foldable phone.

### 2. Overall news sentiment
The supplied sentiment is **neutral**. The AI partnership and discussion of new iPhone products are potential sources of interest, but the summary does not report concrete adoption, sales, or preorder results.

### 3. Why the news is relevant to an investor
The partnership could matter to Apple’s Mac and AI strategy, while the iPhone upgrade-cycle discussion and iPhone Duo coverage relate to potential customer demand. The summary also reports AAPL at **$342.00**, up **2.62% over the past three months**; it does not establish that the news caused that performance.

### 4. Uncertainty or missing information
The summary does not provide details on the partnership’s terms, timing, or expected commercial impact, nor does it report user adoption or iPhone Duo preorder figures. The upgrade-cycle impact is speculative commentary. Broader discussion of AI spending, inflation, and recession risk, and coverage of a Tesla event, are included but their direct relevance to Apple is not specified.

Earnings Analysis:
### AAPL earnings and financial summary

1. **Revenue**
   - Trailing-twelve-month revenue: **$466.8 billion**.
   - No quarterly revenue figure, year-over-year comparison, or revenue-growth rate was provided.

2. **EPS**
   - Recent reported EPS: **$2.02**, versus an estimate of **$1.89**.
   - EPS beat estimates by **6.74%**.

3. **Financial performance**
   - The supplied earnings information indicates an EPS beat, but does not show what drove it.
   - The stock was reported at **$342.00**, up **2.62% over three months**; this is share-price performance, not a measure of the company’s operating results.
   - The Meta–Apple AI partnership and interest in iPhone Duo preorders are reported as news, but no financial impact or sales figures were supplied.

4. **Guidance**
   - **Unavailable.** No company guidance or outlook was provided.

5. **Important missing earnings information**
   - Quarterly revenue and revenue growth
   - Net income and operating income
   - Gross and operating margins
   - Cash flow and balance-sheet details
   - Management commentary or forward guidance

**Bottom line:** AAPL reported EPS above the estimate, and TTM revenue was $466.8 billion. The supplied information is not enough to assess revenue trends, profitability, or the company’s outlook.

) -> dict:
    """Assemble the research package passed to report review."""

    symbol_profile = result.get(
        "symbol_profile",
        {}
    )

    return {
        "symbol": result.get(
            "symbol"
        ),
        "company_name": symbol_profile.get(
            "company_name"
        ),
        "sector": symbol_profile.get(
            "sector"
        ),
        "industry": symbol_profile.get(

        ),

        ),

Part 11. Stage 3 — Evaluator–Optimiser¶

Implements the third workflow pattern: generate, evaluate, refine.

A reviewer scores the report on grounding, completeness, clarity and treatment of limitations. When a report falls below the thresholds, an optimiser rewrites it using the reviewer's specific feedback and the cycle repeats, up to a fixed limit.

Three design decisions are worth noting:

  • The accept decision is made in code. The reviewer supplies scores; the thresholds are applied in Python. A report must clear both an average and a per-criterion minimum.
  • Coverage is checked separately from quality. A report can be well grounded, clear and honest about its gaps while being built on no data at all, and scores alone cannot detect that. An input-coverage check therefore runs alongside the scores, and a coverage failure cannot be rewritten away.
  • The best version is retained, not the last. A revision can score lower than the version it replaced, so the highest-scoring passing iteration is kept, falling back to the highest-scoring iteration when none passed.

The second test deliberately corrupts a draft with invented figures and investment advice, to show the reviewer rejecting a report and the optimiser repairing it. That run is excluded from the agent's memory.

# Evaluation schema. Each criterion is bounded to 0.0-1.0 by the schema,
# so an out-of-range score is rejected rather than silently used.
class ReportEvaluation(BaseModel):
    """Structured quality review of a research report."""

    grounding: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "Every claim is supported by the "
            "specialist analyses."
        )
    )

    completeness: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "All available news, earnings, and market "
            "findings are covered."
        )
    )

    clarity: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "The report is well organized and "
            "easy to read."
        )
    )

    limitations: float = Field(
        ge=0.0,
        le=1.0,
        description=(
            "Missing data and uncertainty are "
            "stated clearly."
        )
    )

    issues: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list
    )

    feedback: list[str] = Field(
        default_factory=list
    )


evaluator_llm = llm.with_structured_output(
    ReportEvaluation
)

# Shared state for the refinement loop.
class ReportReviewState(TypedDict, total=False):
    """Shared state for the Evaluator-Optimizer loop."""

    symbol: str

    # Company reference data. The draft, the evaluator and the optimizer
    # must all see the same grounding surface.
    company_name: str
    sector: str
    industry: str

    # Source material from the research workflow
    news_analysis: str
    earnings_analysis: str
    market_analysis: str

    # Upstream ingestion coverage, used by the input-coverage floor
    article_count: int

    # Report being refined
    report: str
    iteration: int

    # Latest evaluation and all past versions
    evaluation: dict
    history: list

    # Final outputs
    final_report: str
    final_score: float
    final_iteration: int
    final_passed: bool
    final_coverage_issues: list

# Reviewer. Scores the report, then the thresholds and the input-coverage
# check are applied in code to decide acceptance.


EVALUATOR_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are a strict investment research reviewer.

Evaluate the research report for {symbol} against the
specialist analyses and the company reference data below.
Together these are the only source of truth.

COMPANY REFERENCE DATA:
Company name: {company_name}
Sector: {sector}
Industry: {industry}

NEWS ANALYSIS:
{news_analysis}

EARNINGS ANALYSIS:
{earnings_analysis}

MARKET ANALYSIS:
{market_analysis}

REPORT TO EVALUATE:
{report}

Score each criterion from 0.0 to 1.0:

- grounding: every claim in the report is supported by the
  specialist analyses or the company reference data.
  Penalize invented facts and numbers. Do not penalize the
  company name, sector or industry when they match the
  company reference data.
- completeness: the report covers all findings available in
  the news, earnings, and market analyses.
- clarity: the report is well organized, concise, and
  easy for an investor to read.
- limitations: missing data and uncertainty are stated
  clearly.

Rules:
- Do not penalize the report for data that is missing from
  the specialist analyses, as long as the report says the
  data is unavailable.
- Penalize buy, sell, hold, or portfolio advice.
- issues: list each specific problem found in the report.
- feedback: list specific edits that would fix the issues,
  using only the specialist analyses and the company
  reference data.
- Return empty lists when there is nothing to fix.
"""
)


def node_evaluate(
    state: ReportReviewState
) -> dict:
    """Score the current report and collect feedback."""

    prompt = EVALUATOR_PROMPT.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "company_name": state.get(
            "company_name"
        ),
        "sector": state.get(
            "sector"
        ),
        "industry": state.get(
            "industry"
        ),
        "news_analysis": state.get(
            "news_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "earnings_analysis": state.get(
            "earnings_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "market_analysis": state.get(
            "market_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "report": state.get(
            "report",
            ""
        ),
    })

    result = evaluator_llm.invoke(
        prompt
    )

    scores = {
        name: getattr(result, name)
        for name in EVALUATION_CRITERIA
    }

    # The pass decision is made in code, not by the LLM.
    overall = round(
        sum(scores.values()) / len(scores),
        3
    )

    scores_passed = (
        overall >= PASS_SCORE
        and min(scores.values())
        >= MIN_CRITERION_SCORE
    )

    # Input-coverage floor. A report can be perfectly grounded and
    # perfectly honest about what it lacks while still being built on
    # nothing. Scores alone cannot catch that, so check the inputs.
    coverage_issues = []

    article_count = int(
        state.get("article_count") or 0
    )

    if article_count < MIN_ARTICLE_COUNT:
        coverage_issues.append(
            f"Only {article_count} news articles were "
            f"ingested (minimum {MIN_ARTICLE_COUNT}). "
            "The News Analysis has no source material, so "
            "the report cannot be accepted regardless of "
            "its score."
        )

    coverage_ok = not coverage_issues

    passed = scores_passed and coverage_ok

    evaluation = {
        **scores,
        "overall": overall,
        "scores_passed": scores_passed,
        "coverage_ok": coverage_ok,
        "coverage_issues": coverage_issues,
        "passed": passed,
        "issues": result.issues,
        "feedback": result.feedback,
    }

    history = state.get(
        "history",
        []
    ) + [{
        "iteration": state.get(
            "iteration",
            0
        ),
        "report": state.get(
            "report",
            ""
        ),
        **evaluation,
    }]

    return {
        "evaluation": evaluation,
        "history": history,
    }

# Optimiser. Rewrites the report from the reviewer's specific feedback.


OPTIMIZER_PROMPT = ChatPromptTemplate.from_template(
    """
You are the lead Investment Research Agent.

Revise the research report for {symbol} using the
reviewer feedback.

COMPANY REFERENCE DATA:
Company name: {company_name}
Sector: {sector}
Industry: {industry}

NEWS ANALYSIS:
{news_analysis}

EARNINGS ANALYSIS:
{earnings_analysis}

MARKET ANALYSIS:
{market_analysis}

CURRENT REPORT:
{report}

REVIEWER ISSUES:
{issues}

REVIEWER FEEDBACK:
{feedback}

Rules:
- Fix every issue raised by the reviewer.
- Use only facts explicitly contained in the specialist
  analyses or the company reference data.
- Keep the company name, sector and industry when they
  match the company reference data.
- Do not infer missing facts.
- Clearly state when information is unavailable.
- Do not give buy, sell, hold, or portfolio advice.
- Keep these sections: Company, News Analysis,
  Earnings Analysis, Market Analysis, Research Limitations.

Return only the revised report.
"""
)


def node_optimize(
    state: ReportReviewState
) -> dict:
    """Rewrite the report using the evaluator feedback."""

    evaluation = state.get(
        "evaluation",
        {}
    )

    chain = (
        OPTIMIZER_PROMPT
        | llm
        | StrOutputParser()
    )

    result = chain.invoke({
        "symbol": state["symbol"],
        "company_name": state.get(
            "company_name"
        ),
        "sector": state.get(
            "sector"
        ),
        "industry": state.get(
            "industry"
        ),
        "news_analysis": state.get(
            "news_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "earnings_analysis": state.get(
            "earnings_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "market_analysis": state.get(
            "market_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "report": state.get(
            "report",
            ""
        ),
        "issues": "\n".join(
            f"- {item}"
            for item in evaluation.get(
                "issues",
                []
            )
        ),
        "feedback": "\n".join(
            f"- {item}"
            for item in evaluation.get(
                "feedback",
                []
            )
        ),
    })

    return {
        "report": result.strip(),
        "iteration": state.get(
            "iteration",
            0
        ) + 1,
    }
In [46]:
# Accept, refine, or stop. A coverage failure routes straight to finalize:
# rewriting prose cannot create data that was never ingested.
def decide_refinement_step(
    state: ReportReviewState
) -> str:
    """Accept the report or send it back for refinement."""

    evaluation = state["evaluation"]

    if evaluation["passed"]:
        return "accept"

    # Refinement rewrites prose. It cannot create inputs that were never
    # ingested, so a coverage failure goes straight to finalize instead
    # of burning the refinement budget.
    if not evaluation.get("coverage_ok", True):
        return "accept"

    if state.get("iteration", 0) >= MAX_REFINEMENTS:
        return "accept"

    return "refine"


def node_finalize(
    state: ReportReviewState
) -> dict:
    """Keep the highest scoring version of the report."""

    # A refinement can score lower than an earlier version. A version that
    # passed is always preferred over one that did not, even if the failing
    # version has a higher average.
    best = max(
        state["history"],
        key=lambda item: (
            item["passed"],
            item["overall"]
        )
    )

    return {
        "final_report": best["report"],
        "final_score": best["overall"],
        "final_iteration": best["iteration"],
        "final_passed": best["passed"],
        "final_coverage_issues": best.get(
            "coverage_issues",
            []
        ),
    }

# Composes evaluate -> optimise -> evaluate -> finalize, looping on the
# conditional edge until the report is accepted or the limit is reached.
# Build the Evaluator-Optimizer LangGraph workflow

report_review_builder = StateGraph(
    ReportReviewState
)

report_review_builder.add_node(
    "evaluate",
    node_evaluate
)

report_review_builder.add_node(
    "optimize",
    node_optimize
)

report_review_builder.add_node(
    "finalize",
    node_finalize
)

report_review_builder.set_entry_point(
    "evaluate"
)

report_review_builder.add_conditional_edges(
    "evaluate",
    decide_refinement_step,
    {
        "refine": "optimize",
        "accept": "finalize",
    }
)

report_review_builder.add_edge(
    "optimize",
    "evaluate"
)

report_review_builder.add_edge(
    "finalize",
    END
)

report_review_graph = report_review_builder.compile()

print(
    "Evaluator-Optimizer ready: "
    "Evaluate -> (Optimize -> Evaluate)* -> Finalize"
)

Evaluator-Optimizer ready: Evaluate -> (Optimize -> Evaluate)* -> Finalize

def review_and_refine_report(
    research_package: dict,
    write_memory: bool = True
) -> dict:
    """Refine a draft research report until it passes review.

    When write_memory is True the finished run is recorded in the agent's
    memory store. Synthetic or deliberately corrupted drafts should pass
    write_memory=False so they cannot pollute what the agent carries
    forward to later runs.
    """

    result = report_review_graph.invoke({
        "symbol": research_package.get(
            "symbol"
        ),
        "company_name": research_package.get(
            "company_name"
        ),
        "sector": research_package.get(
            "sector"
        ),
        "industry": research_package.get(
            "industry"
        ),
        "news_analysis": research_package.get(
            "news_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "earnings_analysis": research_package.get(
            "earnings_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "market_analysis": research_package.get(
            "market_analysis",
            ""
        ),
        "article_count": research_package.get(
            "article_count",
            0
        ),
        "report": research_package.get(
            "draft_report",
            ""
        ),
        "iteration": 0,
        "history": [],
    })

    result = dict(result)

    if write_memory:
        result["memory_record"] = (
            record_run_memory(
                research_package,
                result
            )
        )

    return result

# Reviewer issues and feedback for each iteration.
# Feedback used at each iteration

def print_evaluation_feedback(
    result: dict
) -> None:
    """Print the evaluator issues and feedback per iteration."""

    for item in result["history"]:

        print("=" * 60)
        print(
            "Iteration:",
            item["iteration"],
            "| Overall:",
            item["overall"],
            "| Passed:",
            item["passed"]
        )

        print("\nIssues:")
        for issue in item["issues"]:
            print("-", issue)

        print("\nFeedback:")
        for feedback in item["feedback"]:
            print("-", feedback)

        print()

# Score by iteration, followed by the retained version.


# Score by iteration

import matplotlib.pyplot as plt


def plot_evaluation_history(
    result: dict,
    title: str
) -> None:
    """Plot the overall evaluator score for each iteration."""

    history = pd.DataFrame(
        result["history"]
    )

    fig, ax = plt.subplots(
        figsize=(7, 4)
    )

    ax.plot(
        history["iteration"],
        history["overall"],
        marker="o",
        label="Overall score"
    )

    ax.axhline(
        PASS_SCORE,
        linestyle="--",
        color="gray",
        label=f"Pass score ({PASS_SCORE})"
    )

    ax.set_xticks(
        history["iteration"]
    )

    ax.set_ylim(0, 1.05)
    ax.set_xlabel("Refinement iteration")
    ax.set_ylabel("Evaluator score")
    ax.set_title(title)
    ax.legend(loc="lower right")

    plt.show()

Part 12. Demonstration — Learning Across Runs¶

Memory is not observable from a single execution, so this part shows the complete cycle: the record written by the review in Part 11, read back by a fresh planning step, and the store growing as a further review is recorded.

The first listing shows every record held for the symbol. Because the memory file persists between executions, it can include records from earlier executions of the notebook as well as the one written in Part 11.

The second step is the substantive one. It calls the planning step directly, prints the notes that step received, and shows the plan produced in response, so that the influence of the earlier run on the later plan can be compared directly.

The third step records a second review of the same research package rather than a new research run. Its purpose is to show the store accumulating and the five-record cap being applied, not a change in the research itself.
