Part 13. Conclusion¶

13.1 Summary¶

The notebook implements an autonomous Investment Research Agent incorporating the three required workflow patterns — prompt chaining, routing, and evaluator–optimiser — together with the four autonomous agent functions: planning, dynamic tool use, self-reflection, and learning across runs. The pipeline executes from end to end without error, and each pattern and function is exercised by a test whose output is retained in this notebook.

13.2 Observations¶

Agent reliability is bounded by the stability of its data sources. During development the Yahoo Finance quote news endpoint began returning an empty list for every symbol while remaining available and raising no error. The news stage consequently received nothing, and the resulting reports contained an empty News Analysis section. Retrieval was restructured to attempt three endpoints in sequence. The broader observation is that an agent whose tools fail silently degrades without signalling that it has degraded.

Plausible-looking output can be produced from no data at all. Before the coverage check was introduced, reports whose News Analysis consisted entirely of statements that no articles were available received evaluator scores between 0.95 and 0.99 and were accepted. The evaluation criteria rewarded candour about missing information, and an empty report satisfies that criterion more easily than a substantive one, because it presents less material to criticise. Scores therefore rose as content fell. Language-model scoring of this kind measures the qualities it is asked about and nothing else, and requires pairing with independent checks on whether the inputs arrived.

Defects upstream of the reasoning layer are difficult to detect from the output. Earnings records were retrieved by selecting the first row of a table sorted with the most recent date first. That table includes quarters that have not yet occurred, which carry an estimate but no reported result. The selection therefore returned an unreported future quarter on every run, and the earnings specialist correctly reported that no results were available. The code raised no error and the report was internally consistent; only comparison against the source table revealed the fault.

Prompts that share a task must share the same permitted evidence. When the report-drafting step was given company reference data that the evaluation step was not, the evaluator identified the resulting sector and industry statements as unsupported and recommended their removal. Extending an agent's evidence in one component requires extending it in every component that judges or revises that output.

Absence of control flow on the failure path is not neutral. The second stage originally advanced unconditionally after retrieval. An invalid symbol therefore produced a complete five-section research report describing a company that does not exist, consuming approximately seven model calls to do so. The first stage had guarded every step against exactly this condition; the second stage had not.

Autonomy is only meaningful where the decision has an effect. The planning component selects which tools to call, and across repeated runs the supplementary retrieval tools it selected contributed no fields that the main pipeline had not already supplied. The selection consumed requests without influencing the result. Similarly, the specialists named in the plan are not used to determine which specialists run.

Constraints requested in a prompt are not constraints. An earlier implementation of run memory asked the model for a single sentence of under forty words and received multi-paragraph responses with headings. Enforcing the limit through a schema and truncating on write produced consistently brief records.

Repeated scoring of equivalent material is not stable. Three reports of substantively identical content received overall scores of 0.95, 0.982 and 0.988 across separate runs during development. A fixed numeric acceptance threshold applied to such scores is therefore sensitive to variation unrelated to report quality.

13.3 Future improvements¶

Control flow. The specialists named in the research plan should determine which specialists execute, through conditional dispatch rather than a fixed sequence. This would make the planning decision consequential and would also remove the need for the separate demonstration routing graph, since routing would occur within the main pipeline.

Earlier failure detection. The input-coverage check currently runs in the third stage, by which point the second stage has already completed. A symbol with price data but no news therefore passes through all three specialists, the draft and the self-assessment before its report is rejected. Applying the same check immediately after retrieval would avoid the intervening model calls.

Caching. Each run retrieves data from Yahoo Finance without reference to previous retrievals, and the tests repeat requests for the same symbols. A response cache keyed by symbol and request type would reduce both latency and exposure to rate limiting.

Stricter coverage thresholds. The present requirement of a single article is weak relative to the five requested. Requiring a larger proportion, and adding a corresponding check that earnings figures represent a reported rather than a forthcoming quarter, would make the coverage test more meaningful.

Reconciliation of the two quality signals. The self-assessment produced in the second stage and the independent evaluation produced in the third scored the same drafts as much as 0.37 apart during development, and a draft the self-assessment marks as not ready for evaluation can still be accepted by the evaluator. Neither value influences the other. Either the self-assessment should gate entry to evaluation or the two should be combined into a single reported measure.

Separation of memory by scope. Records are presently keyed by symbol, so an observation about research method learned on one company is unavailable when analysing another. Methodological notes could be held in a separate store retrieved by semantic similarity, while the per-symbol store continues to provide a numerical baseline for detecting change between runs.

Durable memory. The memory file does not survive a Colab runtime restart. Committing it to the project repository, writing it to mounted storage, or moving it to a small database would allow learning to accumulate across sessions rather than within one.

Calibration of the evaluator. Reports now pass on the first iteration, with at most minor issues raised, so the refinement loop is exercised only by the deliberately corrupted draft. A set of reports with known defects would allow the reviewer's thresholds and criteria to be calibrated against expected outcomes.

Unified execution. The three stages are presently separate graphs joined by intermediate variables. Composing them into a single graph would allow the complete pipeline to be invoked once per symbol and would make the data contracts between stages enforceable in one place.

Correct handling of reporting dates. Earnings dates carry timezone information while the comparison date does not, so the two can disagree by a day around a reporting date. A timezone-aware comparison would remove this edge case.

Evaluation at scale. Results are reported for a small number of large, widely covered technology companies. Extending the tests to smaller companies, other sectors and symbols with sparse news coverage would establish how far the present behaviour generalises.

Part 14. Proposed Expansion: Technical Analysis, Strategy Models, and Evidence Weighting¶

14.1 What the current system does not yet measure¶

The current agent retrieves a three-month window of daily prices, recent earnings, company reference fields, and Yahoo Finance news. It routes these inputs to market, earnings, and news specialists, then evaluates whether the final research report is supported by the retrieved evidence. That pipeline demonstrates planning, tool use, routing, review, and bounded memory, but it is not yet a quantitative investment strategy or a forecasting system. In particular, it does not currently compute technical indicators, detect candlestick formations, compare investment strategies, adjust for market regimes, backtest signals, or validate the market data against independent providers. Its evaluator measures report quality and data coverage, not the future profitability of a research conclusion.

Expanding the project should therefore preserve the existing agent while adding independently testable analytical components. Each new component should expose the observations, time window, source data, confidence, and limitations behind its findings rather than supplying an unsupported buy or sell instruction.

14.2 Chart analytics and candlestick pattern recognition¶

A Technical Analysis Specialist could use timestamped open, high, low, close, and volume (OHLCV) data to generate candlestick charts and calculate indicators. The present three-month closing-price series is insufficient for many of these analyses; the ingestion layer would need longer, explicitly defined price histories and OHLCV fields, with attention to splits, dividends, missing sessions, and market time zones.

Potential analyses include:

Chart feature Proposed measures What it adds Key limitation
Trend 20-, 50-, and 200-day moving averages; moving-average slopes Identifies direction and trend persistence Long windows need more history and lag turning points
Momentum Relative Strength Index (RSI), Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD), rate of change Quantifies price acceleration or loss of momentum Signals can persist at extreme readings
Volatility Average True Range (ATR), Bollinger Bands, rolling standard deviation Describes typical price range and changing volatility Volatility does not indicate direction
Trading participation Volume trends, relative volume, on-balance volume Tests whether price moves coincide with changes in volume Volume quality varies by instrument and venue
Support/resistance Prior swing highs/lows and tested levels Locates historical reaction zones Levels are estimates, not guaranteed barriers
Candlestick formations Hammer, shooting star, doji, engulfing, morning/evening star Produces explicit, inspectable hypotheses about recent price action Pattern labels alone do not establish predictive value

The candlestick detector should use deterministic OHLC rules, report the exact candles and thresholds that triggered a label, and distinguish a detected pattern from a confirmed outcome. For example, a bullish engulfing label should record the two relevant candle bodies and whether the next session supplied confirmation. The chart may visually annotate detected events; an LLM can describe them but should not invent patterns from chart images or substitute a visual impression for a numeric test. All features must be based only on data available at the point being evaluated to avoid look-ahead bias.

14.3 Additional strategies with independent weights¶

The three current specialists organise evidence types (news, earnings, market data); they do not implement competing investment strategies. A subsequent Strategy Analysis Layer could test distinct hypotheses using independently computed scores. Possible modules include trend following (moving-average alignment and trend strength), momentum (relative strength and persistence), mean reversion (deviation from a recent baseline), breakout (movement beyond a previously identified range with volume confirmation), value/quality (valuation, profitability, cash flow, and financial health when those data become available), and event-driven analysis (reported earnings surprises and dated news events). Strategies should specify their intended holding horizon because the same signal may have different implications over days and over months.

Each strategy would produce a standard record containing strategy_name, as_of_timestamp, score, confidence, evidence, data_coverage, and limitations. Scores might use a common bounded scale, such as −1 to +1, but must be calibrated on historical out-of-sample results before comparison. A neutral or missing-data result must remain distinguishable from a genuine zero signal.

An initial, illustrative allocation of analytical influence, not a validated allocation of capital, could be:

Component Existing or proposed Example weight
Earnings and fundamental evidence Existing specialist, extended with financial statements 20%
News and event evidence Existing specialist 15%
Market-price summary Existing specialist 15%
Chart indicators and candlestick analytics Proposed technical specialist 20%
Independent strategy ensemble (trend, momentum, mean reversion, breakout) Proposed strategy layer 20%
Macro and sector conditions Proposed contextual specialist 10%
Total 100%

These weights are examples to test, not performance claims. Price summaries, technical indicators, and trend strategies all use overlapping market data; their signals are correlated, so treating them as independent evidence can overstate confidence. An implementation should measure correlations, ablate individual modules, cap redundant contributions, and recalibrate weights against held-out periods. Missing inputs should trigger a coverage warning and an explicit no-score or partial-score policy, not automatic redistribution that conceals the gap. A separate risk and data-integrity gate should be able to block interpretation of any composite regardless of its numerical score.

14.4 Expansion of data sources and risk analysis¶

The existing Yahoo-only design creates a single-provider dependency. Cross-checking earnings dates, historical OHLCV, corporate actions, and current quotes against another documented source would help identify silent source errors. Additional inputs could include audited filings and financial statements, sector benchmarks, benchmark indices, Treasury yields, inflation and employment releases, and a reliable economic-event calendar. Every record should retain source, retrieval time, exchange time zone, period covered, and whether the figure was originally reported or subsequently revised.

A dedicated Risk Specialist could report maximum drawdown, realized volatility, market beta, downside deviation, liquidity and concentration limits, and the effect of transaction costs and slippage on hypothetical strategies. This component should be a constraint or veto rather than simply another weighted source of positive sentiment. Data gaps, stale quotes, detected future information, or unrealistic execution assumptions should lead to an explicit warning or refusal to score.

14.5 Testing whether the expansion works¶

The next phase should distinguish three evaluation targets. Data integrity checks whether retrieval, adjustments, timestamps, and source coverage are correct. Research quality checks whether the report faithfully represents available data, retaining the existing independent coverage gate. Strategy performance is a separate evaluation against future outcomes that were not available at the time of signal generation.

Before giving strategy scores operational significance, the project would require chronological train/validation/test splits, walk-forward backtests, realistic fees and slippage, survivorship-bias controls, prevention of look-ahead leakage, and comparison with simple buy-and-hold or benchmark baselines. Results should include returns alongside drawdown, turnover, Sharpe-like risk-adjusted measures, and uncertainty estimates. Test periods should include uptrends, drawdowns, sideways markets, and different sectors. Candlestick detections should be assessed for precision and predictive usefulness, not judged by how plausible their names sound. The system should log the contribution of every strategy so that removing a module can reveal whether it truly improves out-of-sample performance.

14.6 Practical implementation sequence¶

  1. Extend ingestion to several years of adjusted daily OHLCV and add provenance, data-freshness checks, and an optional second source.
  2. Add technical charting with computed indicators, candlestick rules, plotted signals, and unit tests for each feature.
  3. Add a strategy registry whose modules return schema-validated evidence and separate scores; preserve the existing three specialists unchanged at first.
  4. Introduce a transparent aggregation step with versioned configurable weights, missing-data rules, disagreement reporting, and a risk gate; keep evaluator quality scores separate from strategy scores.
  5. Backtest and calibrate on historical data without look-ahead leakage, then use walk-forward validation and compare each added module with the original system.
  6. Integrate conditional planning so the agent invokes only the modules justified by the question, available inputs, and investment horizon, and stores outcomes separately from its short per-symbol research notes.

This roadmap extends the notebook from evidence-grounded report generation toward a testable multi-strategy research platform. Until those modules are implemented and validated, the present project should be described as an investment research assistant, not a trading system with demonstrated predictive performance.

AI Usage Disclosure¶

Generative AI tools were used during the development of this project as an assistant to the team. All AI-assisted output was reviewed, tested and, where necessary, corrected by the authors, who take responsibility for the code, the design decisions and the results reported in this notebook.

This section covers AI assistance used to build the project. It is separate from the language model the agent itself calls at run time (LLM_MODEL, through the OpenAI API), which is a component of the system described above.

Area How AI assistance was used
Code assistance Suggesting and completing code, explaining errors and tracebacks, and proposing fixes. Examples include the retry and fallback structure for Yahoo Finance requests, JSON-safe handling of NaN values, extending the price window from one month to three months, and corrections found during review: routing symbols with no news to the coverage check, supplying revenue to the earnings specialist, retaining a passing report over a higher-scoring failing one, and enforcing the required tool in code.
Python library lookup Looking up APIs and usage for yfinance (price history, info, earnings_dates, news and search), LangGraph (StateGraph, conditional edges, state merging), LangChain (ChatPromptTemplate, with_structured_output, @tool), Pydantic field constraints, and pandas. Suggested usage was checked against the installed library versions by running the code.
Multi-agent design Discussing how to structure the workflow patterns (prompt chaining, routing and evaluator–optimiser), how to divide work between the planner and the news, earnings and market specialists, what each shared state should contain, where decisions should be made in code rather than by the model, and how run memory should feed the planner. Final design choices were made by the team.
Documentation Drafting and editing markdown sections, code comments and docstrings, and reviewing the notebook for inconsistencies between the documentation, the code and the recorded outputs.

AI tools were not used to generate the market data, news or evaluation results shown in this notebook; those are produced by executing the code.
